prize_parts.citation: For the design of ionizable lipid nanoparticles, from nucleic-acid entrapment to pH-triggered release, that enables the delivery of nucleic-acid medicines

statement.case_for: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles remain my preferred single part. The achievement is a molecular design principle: a lipid that is neutral in blood and charged in the acidic endosome, combined with controlled self-assembly, allows a polyanionic nucleic acid to be entrapped, protected and then released inside the cell. That is synthetic and physical chemistry, and the consequences, approved siRNA therapy and mRNA vaccines at global scale, are the most thoroughly validated on the shortlist. The 2023 Medicine prize honoured the nucleoside modification of the cargo, not the vehicle that lets it work. I have changed my credited trio. In round 1 I wanted Anderson beside Cullis and Hope. Sparr, Chabes and Aqvist all place the decisive ionizable-lipid concept, entrapment and bilayer physical chemistry in Vancouver, and lipidoid libraries are a later screening strategy that broadened the chemical space but did not create the principle. A citation limited to entrapment and pH-triggered release is narrow enough that Cullis, Hope and Madden are the defensible trio, and it also gives the committee the narrowly defined achievement that Somfai and Zou said they would need. I now also see that three members (Aqvist, Chabes, Sparr) independently named this same trio, which is a coincidence of scientific judgment rather than a count I rely on.
statement.case_against: Attribution is still the weak point. MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer have real claims that a three-name limit excludes, and the industrial SNALP development and patent history could make any trio look arbitrary. Brzezinski, Somfai and Zou are right that the discovery is a line of work and not a single event, and some will read it as pharmaceutical formulation rather than chemistry. The 2023 Medicine prize may also make a related Chemistry prize look partly redundant. If the committee cannot agree on the narrow citation, I do not insist on B016 over a cleaner option.

responses.point: The Vancouver work of Cullis, Hope and Madden on entrapment, ionizable lipids and formulation is the molecular foundation of later siRNA and mRNA products, and Anderson should not be assumed to belong by default.
responses.response: You have persuaded me on the trio. I conceded Anderson's lipidoid work as a screening strategy that came later, and I now credit Madden rather than Anderson, since entrapment and bilayer phase behaviour were Vancouver work. I would still ask that the citation text say clearly that it covers the ionizable-lipid design principle and not the whole delivery field. That keeps your pKa-dependent charge and bilayer-to-non-bilayer framing at the centre without pretending to settle the lipidoid and industrial strands.

responses.point: Somfai would support B016 if the committee can agree on a narrowly defined achievement, ionizable lipid design for nucleic acid encapsulation, with a clean trio, and notes B011 is a cleaner but less novel case.
responses.response: I have taken your condition literally. The citation now names entrapment and pH-triggered release, and the trio is Cullis, Hope and Madden, which is the set that Aqvist, Chabes and Sparr also arrived at independently. On B011, I accept that C-N coupling needed its own ligand and mechanistic solutions and that Kosugi is a precursor. My remaining difficulty is comparative: the 2010 prize rewarded the central logic of palladium catalysis, whereas no prize has recognised the delivery chemistry. I would call B011 the safest fallback but not the most consequential choice.

responses.point: Brzezinski treats B016 as a line of work with six names for three slots, and would support it only if an expert report resolves who made the decisive ionizable-lipid step.
responses.response: Your procedural point is fair, and I do not claim the field is a single moment. I think the decisive step can be stated: the ionizable-lipid and entrapment principle that made efficient encapsulation and endosomal release possible, which is Vancouver work. That is why I dropped the lipidoid line from the trio rather than defending a six-person narrative. I also disagree gently with pairing B027 with B008. Both parts are well defined, but a retrospective mechanistic prize and a recent engineering prize do not make the coherent story you need, and I still prefer one part with clear consequences.

responses.point: Chabes holds B008 as the first choice with Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, citing independent reproduction and clinical use, but accepts B016 as a strong alternative with the Vancouver trio.
responses.response: I agree on the Vancouver trio and I am glad the two of us have converged on it. On B008, I proposed Liu, Komor and Gaudelli at the opening because Komor and Gaudelli did the hands-on work on the cytosine and adenine editors. I still believe the clean attribution is a strength, and I keep B008 as my first alternative. My reservation is that it follows the 2020 genome-editing prize and the clinical record, bystander editing and off-target deamination, is still short. If the committee prefers B008, I would argue for the three-name credit over Liu alone, because Linke and Brzezinski's single-name version omits the people who built the editors.

responses.point: Aqvist prefers B009 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa as a new pharmacological modality, and asks whether the 2023 Medicine prize has taken the urgency from rewarding the delivery vehicle.
responses.response: On urgency, I would say the opposite: the mRNA prize shows the vehicle was needed and went unrecognised, so the chemistry is the unrewarded half of the same story. On B009, I still see a genuinely new modality, but Aqvist's own reservation holds for me too. No degrader is widely approved and PROTACs and cereblon glues are historically different discoveries, so one citation risks looking like two prizes. I keep B009 as an alternative, which is a bet on a prize a few years from now.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a narrowly worded ionizable-lipid citation that credits Cullis, Hope and Madden while leaving out MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer
Whether delivery chemistry will be read as a chemistry discovery rather than pharmaceutical formulation
Whether the 2023 Medicine prize makes a related Chemistry prize look redundant
Priority and patent history between the academic Vancouver work and industrial SNALP development, which I cannot resolve from the committee record
Whether the clinical record for B009 or B008 will mature enough to overtake B016 within a year or two
statement.conflict_note: No conflict has arisen since round 1. I have no recorded tie to the Vancouver, Alnylam or MIT groups, or to the B008, B009 or B011 candidates. My only overlap is topical, with Emma Sparr's work on lipid and peptide self-assembly and my own nanoparticle and peptide work, and I do not consider it a recusal issue.
